value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: The Employment Act applies in full to manual workers whatever their wage (First Schedule para 1, as substituted from 1 Jan 2023), including in agricultural undertakings. Estate workers paid by the day are guaranteed work on at least 24 days a month (s. 16). Act 446 sets housing and amenity standards for estates over 20 ha. Peninsular only; Sabah and Sarawak have their own Labour Ordinances.
source: Employment Act 1955 ss. 2, 60K (Act A1651, 2022); Sabah Labour Ordinance (Cap. 67) · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf

value_label: The national statutory minimum wage applies
note: The national minimum wage (RM1,700 a month from 1 Feb 2025; from 1 Aug 2025 for employers with fewer than five workers) applies with no exclusion for agriculture or for foreign workers. Piece-rate and tonnage workers must also receive at least RM1,700.
source: National Wages Consultative Council Act 2011 (Act 732); Minimum Wages Order 2024 · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/2541500/PUA%20376.pdf

value_label: Statutory limits on hours apply
note: Limits of 8 hours a day and 45 a week (lowered from 48 by Act A1651) apply, with no exclusion for agriculture. The Director General may allow longer hours on application (s. 60A(1A)), and the Minister may exempt by order (s. 2B).
source: Employment Act 1955 s. 60A (as amended 2022) · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf

value_label: Cannot change without the employer's consent
note: Each employer needs the Director General's prior approval to employ a foreign employee (Employment Act s. 60K), and must report when the worker leaves, absconding included (s. 60KA). A pass stops being valid once its conditions are breached (Immigration Act s. 55B(2)). The rule tying the Visit Pass (Temporary Employment) to one employer, and any transfer procedure, sit in the Immigration Regulations 1963 and in Immigration Department practice, neither readable on the trusted sites. Ministry page
source: Immigration Act 1959/63; Immigration Regulations 1963; Immigration Department guidance · official guidance: https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/perkhidmatan-utama/pekerja-asing-2/

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: Non-citizens may join a union but may not be, or act as, members of a union executive (s. 28(1)(a)) or be employed by a union (s. 29(2)(a)). LOM lists a 12 Jan 2024 instrument for this Act that could not be opened.
source: Trade Unions Act 1959 (Act 262), as amended 2024 · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/16547_BI/001%20-%20Act%20262.pdf

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Agencies may charge a non-citizen employee no more than one month's basic wage as a placement fee; if the employer pays, nothing may be taken from the worker (s. 14B(3)). Overcharging is an offence (s. 28). Fees charged in sending states are outside the Act.
source: Private Employment Agencies Act 1981 (Act 246), as amended 2017; National Action Plan on Forced Labour 2021–2025 · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3165320_BI/Act%20246%20(REPRINT%202018).pdf

value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: Covered by SOCSO as employees in an industry. The Act excludes only foreign workers without a valid pass (First Schedule para (12A)). The date foreign workers were brought in (reported as 2019) and the schemes that apply were not confirmed from the texts read. Act A1788 (2026, not yet in force) adds non-employment injury cover, which a foreign worker loses for misusing a pass.
source: Employees' Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4); PERKESO, foreign workers scheme · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3226981_BI/Act%204%20(Online%202026).pdf

value_label: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
note: General Department of Labour offices and an online complaint system; plantations are often remote, and complaints require the worker's pass to be valid.
source: Department of Labour (JTKSM)

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: No route was found in the texts read. Permanent residence (Entry Permit, s. 10) is at the Director General's discretion; maximum stay rules for foreign workers sit in policy and regulations not readable on the trusted sites.
source: Immigration Act 1959/63; Ministry of Home Affairs policy · official guidance: https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/perkhidmatan-utama/pekerja-asing-2/

value_label: Barred
note: Reported to be barred: Visit Pass (Temporary Employment) holders may not bring dependants. This could not be confirmed from any text on LOM.
source: Immigration Department, conditions of the PLKS · official guidance: https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/perkhidmatan-utama/pekerja-asing-2/

value_label: A labor statute applies with exclusions, or a sector-specific labor statute applies
note: The Employment Act covers domestic employees ('domestic servant' until Act A1651, in force 1 Jan 2023), but the First Schedule disapplies ss. 12, 14, 16, 22, 58A, 60, 60A–60F, 60FA, 60I, 61 and 64 and Parts IX (maternity) and XIIA (termination benefits). Part XI allows termination on 14 days' notice. Sabah and Sarawak have their own Labour Ordinances.
source: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule para. 2; Act A1651 (2022) · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf

value_label: No wage floor
note: The Minimum Wages Order 2024 (RM1,700 a month) does not apply to domestic servants. No other legal wage floor was found; pay floors set in bilateral arrangements with sending states are not in Malaysian law. The Order still says 'domestic servant', although the Act has said 'domestic employee' since 2023.
source: Minimum Wages Order 2024; Malaysia–Indonesia MOU on domestic workers, 1 April 2022 · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/2541500/PUA%20376.pdf

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: Since 1 Jan 2023 the weekly rest day (s. 59) applies, as Part XII is no longer excluded as a whole. Hours limits (s. 60A), pay for rest-day work (s. 60), holidays, annual leave and sick leave (ss. 60D–60F) remain excluded. Before 2023 all of Part XII was excluded.
source: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule para. 2 · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf

value_label: Cannot change without the employer's consent
note: Each employer needs the Director General's prior approval to employ a foreign employee (Employment Act s. 60K), and must report when the worker leaves, absconding included (ss. 57A, 57B). A pass stops being valid once its conditions are breached (Immigration Act s. 55B(2)). The rule tying the Visit Pass (Temporary Employment) to one employer, and any transfer procedure, sit in the Immigration Regulations 1963 and in Immigration Department practice, neither readable on the trusted sites. Ministry
source: Immigration Department guidance · official guidance: https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/perkhidmatan-utama/pembantu-rumah-asing/

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: Non-citizens may join a union but may not be, or act as, members of a union executive (s. 28(1)(a)) or be employed by a union (s. 29(2)(a)). For live-in domestic workers, membership is also limited in practice. LOM lists a 12 Jan 2024 instrument for this Act that could not be opened.
source: Trade Unions Act 1959 (Act 262) · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/16547_BI/001%20-%20Act%20262.pdf

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Agencies may charge a non-citizen employee no more than one month's basic wage as a placement fee, plus no other fees beyond the First Schedule. If the employer pays, nothing may be taken from the worker (s. 14B(3)). Licence B covers foreign domestic servants. Fees charged in sending states are outside the Act.
source: Private Employment Agencies Act 1981 (Act 246); Malaysia–Indonesia MOU 2022 · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3165320_BI/Act%20246%20(REPRINT%202018).pdf

value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: The First Schedule exclusion of domestic servants (para (3)) was deleted from 1 Jun 2021, which brings them within SOCSO. The deleted wording was checked in the 2016 Malay text. Only foreign workers without a valid pass are excluded (para (12A)). Which benefits apply to foreign domestic workers was not confirmed from an official text (for example, employment injury only).
source: Employees' Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4); PERKESO announcement, 2021 · official text: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/1702260/PUA%20247.pdf

value_label: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
note: General channels only; the worker lives in the employer's home.
source: Department of Labour (JTKSM)

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: No route was found in the texts read. Permanent residence (Entry Permit, s. 10) is at the Director General's discretion, and the Act does not count time on a temporary employment pass. Stay limits and pass conditions sit in the Immigration Regulations 1963 and Immigration Department policy, which could not be read on the trusted sites.
source: Immigration Act 1959/63 · official guidance: https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/perkhidmatan-utama/pembantu-rumah-asing/

value_label: Barred
note: Reported to be barred: Visit Pass (Temporary Employment) holders may not bring dependants, and pass conditions reportedly bar marriage in Malaysia and pregnancy. None of this appears in any text found on LOM, since the principal Immigration Regulations 1963 are not online there.
source: Immigration Department guidance · official guidance: https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/perkhidmatan-utama/pembantu-rumah-asing/

value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: The Employment Act applies; construction workers and machine operators are listed 'workmen' (First Schedule), and Part 4 (rest days, hours) applies to workmen earning up to $4,500 a month (s. 35(a)). Work permit conditions add obligations on top.
source: Employment Act 1968 s. 2, Part IV · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968?WholeDoc=1

value_label: No wage floor
note: No statutory minimum wage; none was found in the Employment Act. Progressive Wage requirements were not checked in text.
source: Employment Act 1968; MOM, Progressive Wage Model · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/progressive-wage-model/what-is-pwm

value_label: Statutory limits on hours apply
note: Employment Act Part 4 applies to these workmen: no more than 8 hours a day or 44 a week (s. 38(1)) and one rest day a week (s. 36(1)).
source: Employment Act 1968 ss. 38, 35 · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968?WholeDoc=1

value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: The worker may work only for the employer and sector named in the permit (Part VI para. 1); the new employer must apply for a new permit (EFMA s. 7). The rule that a transfer needs the current employer's consent was not found in statute.
source: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act 1990; MOM guidance · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-worker/sector-specific-rules/hiring-an-existing-manufacturing-or-services-worker

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: Any person over 16 may be a union member (s. 28(1)). Non-citizens may not act as union officers without the Minister's approval (s. 30(3)).
source: Trade Unions Act 1940, s. 30 · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/TUA1940?WholeDoc=1

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Same cap as for all foreign employees: one month's salary per year of work pass or contract, maximum two months (r. 12(1)(a)); costs outside Singapore excluded (r. 12(2)). Agencies may charge employers without limit (r. 12(3)).
source: Employment Agencies Act 1958 and Rules; Work Passes Regulations 2012, Fourth Schedule · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/EAA1958-S172-2011?WholeDoc=1

value_label: Only employer-bought private or accident insurance is required
note: Employer must buy medical insurance (Part IV para. 4), enrol the worker in a Primary Care Plan (para. 4A, from Dec 2023) and insure against work-injury liability (WICA s. 24). MediShield Life covers only citizens and permanent residents (s. 3(3)).
source: Work Injury Compensation Act 2019; Work Passes Regulations 2012 · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/WICA2019?WholeDoc=1

value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: Mandatory mediation by the Commissioner, then the Employment Claims Tribunal (ECA s. 3). Any dedicated migrant worker channel could not be checked.
source: MOM; Migrant Workers' Centre · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/eservices/fwmomcare

value_label: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
note: Permanent residence is at the Controller's discretion (IA s. 10); no statutory bar found. Marriage to a citizen or PR needs prior approval (Part VI para. 6). Moving to an S Pass, which may lead to PR, is possible in policy but not shown in statute.
source: MOM, Work Permit and S Pass eligibility; ICA, permanent residence · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/faq/s-pass/how-do-i-convert-a-work-permit-to-an-s-pass

value_label: Barred
note: A dependant's pass for spouse or child of any work pass holder is discretionary (Immigration Regulations reg. 11(1)); the exclusion of work permit holders is policy. Marriage to a citizen or PR needs approval and pregnancy in Singapore is barred (Part VI paras 6-7).
source: Work Passes Regulations 2012, Fourth Schedule · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/dependants-pass/eligibility

value_label: Only administrative regulations under a non-labor statute apply
note: The Employment Act excludes domestic workers from 'employee' (s. 2). Terms are set as work permit conditions in the Work Passes Regulations under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (Fourth Schedule Parts I-II), not by a labor statute.
source: Employment Act 1968 s. 2; Work Passes Regulations 2012, Fourth Schedule Part I · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968?WholeDoc=1

value_label: No wage floor
note: Singapore has no statutory minimum wage; none was found in the Employment Act. The employer must pay at least the salary declared in the work permit application (Fourth Schedule Part I para. 7), which is a contractual figure, not a floor.
source: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act 1990 · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/progressive-wage-model/what-is-pwm

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: No limit on hours: Employment Act Part 4 does not apply. The employer must grant 'adequate rest daily' and one rest day in every 7 days, which may be replaced or paid out by written agreement provided at least one rest day a month is kept (Fourth Schedule Part I paras 10-13B, from 1 Jan 2023).
source: Work Passes Regulations 2012, Fourth Schedule · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/EFMA1990-S569-2012?WholeDoc=1

value_label: Cannot change without the employer's consent
note: The worker may work only for the employer named in the permit (Part VI para. 1) and a new permit must be applied for by the new employer (EFMA s. 7). The rule that a transfer needs the current employer's consent was not found in statute.
source: MOM, transfer of migrant domestic workers · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/transfer-to-a-new-employer

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: Any person over 16 may be a union member (s. 28(1)), and 'workman' covers anyone under a contract of service. Non-citizens may not act as union officers without the Minister's approval (s. 30(3)).
source: Trade Unions Act 1940 · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/TUA1940?WholeDoc=1

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Licensed agencies may charge a foreign worker at most one month's salary per year of the work pass or contract (whichever is shorter), up to two months' salary (r. 12(1)(a)). Costs incurred outside Singapore are excluded from the cap (r. 12(2)). Employers may not take kickbacks from agencies (Fourth Schedule Part I para. 19).
source: Employment Agencies Rules · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/EAA1958-S172-2011?WholeDoc=1

value_label: Only employer-bought private or accident insurance is required
note: Employer must buy medical insurance for in-patient and day-surgery costs (Part II para. 4) and personal accident insurance of at least $60,000 (para. 4A). Domestic workers are not covered by the Work Injury Compensation Act (Third Schedule item 3), and MediShield Life covers only citizens and permanent residents (s. 3(3)).
source: Work Passes Regulations 2012 · official text: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/EFMA1990-S569-2012?WholeDoc=1

value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: The Centre for Domestic Employees helpline and MOM's helpline for domestic workers, in several languages.
source: MOM; Centre for Domestic Employees

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: Permanent residence requires an entry permit issued at the Controller's discretion (IA s. 10); no statutory bar on work permit holders was found. Marriage to a citizen or PR needs the Controller's prior approval (Part VI para. 6). That work permit holders are not eligible for PR is policy.
source: MOM; ICA · official guidance: https://www.ica.gov.sg/reside/PR/apply

value_label: Barred
note: The Immigration Regulations allow a dependant's pass for the spouse or child of any work pass holder at the Controller's discretion (reg. 11(1)), so the bar is policy, not statute. Work permit holders may not marry a citizen or PR without approval or become pregnant in Singapore (Part VI paras 6-7).
source: Work Passes Regulations 2012, Fourth Schedule · official guidance: https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/dependants-pass/eligibility

value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: The Labour Protection Act applies to all employees regardless of nationality; domestic workers and farm and fishing workers are covered by ministerial regulations instead.
source: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s. 22

value_label: The national statutory minimum wage applies
note: The provincial minimum wages set by the Wage Committee apply to migrant workers.
source: Labour Protection Act s. 79; Wage Committee notifications

value_label: Statutory limits on hours apply
note: Normal hours of at most 8 a day and 48 a week, with a weekly holiday.
source: Labour Protection Act ss. 23, 28

value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: Same rule as for other MOU workers: leaving before the contract ends bars work for another employer unless the employer was at fault or damages (pro-rata recruitment costs) are paid; a new job must start within 30 days. Not applicable to renewed contracts. Ministry rules for registered (non-MOU) workers were not checked. Official guidance: Grounds-based mobility. The five grounds are: the employer dismisses or dies; goes bankrupt; abuses or assaults the worker; breaches the contract or labour-protection law; or the work is dangerous to life or health. Workers who entered before 16 Aug 2016 may change employer.
source: Royal Ordinance on the Management of Employment of Foreign Workers B.E. 2560 (2017), as amended 2018; Department of Employment notification · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/aWFRTmVvOWUvdzZlVnJ4MUFPTmhEUT09

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: May join a union, but only Thai nationals may found one (s. 88), and committee members must be Thai by birth (s. 101). The Act does not exclude agricultural employers.
source: Labour Relations Act B.E. 2518 (1975) ss. 88, 101 · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/RjlYQUc2ZGMyeHBKMmRhZjdjRS9wUT09

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are prohibited in the destination's law
note: Licensed recruiters may take service fees and costs only from employers, at rates set by the Director-General, and nothing from the worker. An employer who recruits directly may not collect recruitment-related money from the worker, except passport, health check, work permit and similar costs it advanced. These may be deducted at no more than 10% of monthly pay. Breach of s. 42 is a crime (s. 111).
source: Royal Ordinance B.E. 2560 (2017), as amended 2018 · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/aWFRTmVvOWUvdzZlVnJ4MUFPTmhEUT09

value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: Registered workers in formal employment are enrolled in the Social Security Fund and the Workmen's Compensation Fund.
source: Social Security Act B.E. 2533; Workmen's Compensation Act B.E. 2537

value_label: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
note: Hotline 1694 (Department of Employment) and 1546 (Department of Labour Protection and Welfare) with interpretation, and migrant worker assistance centers.
source: Department of Employment; Department of Labour Protection and Welfare

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: As for fishers: temporary stay tied to the work permit (up to one year at a time, extendable), permanent residence only within the annual quota and Committee criteria; no provision found counting time as an MOU or registered worker.
source: Royal Ordinance B.E. 2560 (2017); Thailand–Myanmar, –Cambodia and –Laos MOUs · official guidance: https://www.doe.go.th/prd/alien/news/param/site/152/cat/7/sub/0/pull/detail/view/detail/object_id/107070

value_label: Barred
note: Workers may not bring dependants under the memorandum system; children born in Thailand may be registered.
source: Ministry of Labour; Ministry of Interior

value_label: A labor statute applies with exclusions, or a sector-specific labor statute applies
note: A ministerial regulation applies parts of the Labour Protection Act to agricultural work, mainly to workers employed year-round; seasonal workers have fewer protections.
source: Ministerial Regulation on Labour Protection in Agricultural Work B.E. 2557 (2014)

value_label: A separate floor applies that is lower than, or not linked to, the national minimum
note: The minimum wage applies to workers covered by the regulation; for seasonal and piece-rate workers the floor is less clear (to confirm).
source: Ministerial Regulation on Agricultural Work B.E. 2557 (2014)

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: The regulation sets rest periods and a weekly holiday, but no limit on daily hours.
source: Ministerial Regulation on Agricultural Work B.E. 2557 (2014)

value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: Same rule as for other MOU workers: leaving before the contract ends bars work for another employer unless the employer was at fault or damages (pro-rata recruitment costs) are paid; a new job must start within 30 days. Not applicable to renewed contracts. Ministry rules for registered (non-MOU) workers were not checked. Official guidance: This covers general (non-MOU-imported) foreign workers. A separate FAQ (object 192) says they can apply without waiting for the old employer's exit notice, and FAQ 189 adds a 1,000-baht fee for domestic and labourer jobs. MOU-recruited farm workers follow the 5-ground rule (TH-MOU).
source: Royal Ordinance B.E. 2560 (2017) · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/aWFRTmVvOWUvdzZlVnJ4MUFPTmhEUT09

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: May join a union, but only Thai nationals may found one (s. 88), and committee members must be Thai by birth (s. 101). The Act does not exclude agricultural employers.
source: Labour Relations Act B.E. 2518 (1975) · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/RjlYQUc2ZGMyeHBKMmRhZjdjRS9wUT09

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are prohibited in the destination's law
note: Licensed recruiters may take service fees and costs only from employers, at rates set by the Director-General, and nothing from the worker. An employer who recruits directly may not collect recruitment-related money from the worker, except passport, health check, work permit and similar costs it advanced. These may be deducted at no more than 10% of monthly pay. Breach of s. 42 is a crime (s. 111).
source: Royal Ordinance B.E. 2560 (2017) · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/aWFRTmVvOWUvdzZlVnJ4MUFPTmhEUT09

value_label: Only employer-bought private or accident insurance is required
note: Social security and work-injury compensation apply without a nationality condition, but employees of cultivation and livestock businesses that do not employ workers all year, and seasonal or casual workers, are excluded from social security.
source: Social Security Act B.E. 2533 s. 4 and Royal Decree on exclusions · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/Yi83NFhZaWZwaUxacnpFY3NRRWxSUT09

value_label: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
note: General hotlines; farms are dispersed and inspections few.
source: Department of Labour Protection and Welfare

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: No route to permanent residence.
source: Royal Ordinance B.E. 2560 (2017)

value_label: Barred
note: May not bring dependants.
source: Ministry of Labour

value_label: A labor statute applies with exclusions, or a sector-specific labor statute applies
note: The Labour Protection Act applies only in part: the Sea Fishery Regulation 2022 replaces it except for listed sections (general provisions, wage payment ss. 76-77, s. 89, complaints, welfare fund, inspectors, notices). The Work in Fishing Act 2019 adds sector-specific duties of vessel owners.
source: Work in Fishing Act B.E. 2562 (2019); Ministerial Regulation on Sea Fishing Work B.E. 2557 (2014), as amended · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/QzAyeDJLV3RJWmVlUCtnOUthRU0xZz09

value_label: The national statutory minimum wage applies
note: Fishers must be paid a monthly wage of at least the daily minimum wage set by the Wage Committee times 30, at least once a month (catch shares at least every three months), through the worker's bank account at the employer's cost.
source: Ministerial Regulation on Sea Fishing Work, as amended 2018 · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/QzAyeDJLV3RJWmVlUCtnOUthRU0xZz09

value_label: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
note: At least 10 hours of rest in any 24 and 77 hours in any 7 days, with records for inspectors; in emergencies rest may be interrupted with compensatory rest. The LPA hours limits (s. 23, 8 a day, 48 a week) are not among the sections the Regulation keeps, so there is no limit on hours as such.
source: Ministerial Regulation on Sea Fishing Work; Work in Fishing Act B.E. 2562 · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/QzAyeDJLV3RJWmVlUCtnOUthRU0xZz09

value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: A worker who leaves before the contract ends may not work for another employer unless he proves to the registrar that the employer was at fault, or pays the former employer damages (the recruitment costs, pro rata to time served); he must then start with the new employer within 30 days or the work permit and stay end. The restriction does not apply during a renewed contract. Cabinet rules on transfers for registered (non-MOU) fishers sit on ministry pages and were not checked.
source: Royal Ordinance B.E. 2560 (2017) · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/aWFRTmVvOWUvdzZlVnJ4MUFPTmhEUT09

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: Migrant workers may be members of a union (s. 95 sets no nationality condition), but only Thai nationals may found one (s. 88) and committee members must be Thai by birth (s. 101).
source: Labour Relations Act B.E. 2518 (1975) · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/RjlYQUc2ZGMyeHBKMmRhZjdjRS9wUT09

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are prohibited in the destination's law
note: Recruitment service fees and costs for fishers are to be charged to the vessel owner, who must pay them. In general, licensed recruiters may not take money from the worker, and an employer who recruits directly may not collect recruitment-related money from the worker, except passport, health check, work permit and similar costs it advanced, deductible at no more than 10% of monthly pay.
source: Work in Fishing Act B.E. 2562 (2019) · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/OFl5b0Q5Q3cybnFmL1NTYlRqbHZaUT09

value_label: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
note: The Social Security Act covers employees aged 15-60 without a nationality condition, and the Workmen's Compensation Act covers fishing employers. Fishing businesses that do not employ workers all year are excluded from social security. Vessel owners must also provide health and welfare benefits set by the Labour Minister (insurance or other means).
source: Workmen's Compensation Act B.E. 2537; Social Security Act B.E. 2533 · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/Yi83NFhZaWZwaUxacnpFY3NRRWxSUT09

value_label: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
note: General complaint route to labour inspectors (LPA s. 123, kept for sea fishing by cl. 3). Vessels fishing outside Thai waters must give crew satellite messaging or calls (at least 10 MB or 15 minutes a month), and every vessel must post the numbers of the Department of Fisheries and Seafarer Help. Retaliation against complainants is barred, and disputes go to the Labour Court. A multilingual migrant hotline (if any) sits on ministry pages and was not checked.
source: Department of Fisheries; Department of Labour Protection and Welfare · official text: https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/QzAyeDJLV3RJWmVlUCtnOUthRU0xZz09

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: No route to permanent residence.
source: Royal Ordinance B.E. 2560 (2017)

value_label: Barred
note: May not bring dependants.
source: Ministry of Labour

value_label: The general labor statute applies in full
note: Construction and agricultural workers are "employees" and, if manual, "workmen" under the Employment Act. Only seamen, domestic workers and managerial, executive or confidential staff are excluded. Domestic workers (BN-DW) differ: value 1.
source: Employment Order 2009 · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cap-278-2026-ed-employment-act.pdf

value_label: No wage floor
note: The Minimum Wage Order covers only employees in the sectors listed in Schedule 1: banking, finance, ICT, telecoms and, since 1 April 2025, land survey, securities, private medical and education, security guards, tourism, travel agencies, architecture/engineering/QS firms and insurance. Construction contractors and agriculture are not listed.
source: Minimum Wage Order 2023 · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/S-4-2025-EMPLOYMENT-MINIMUM-WAGE-AMENDMENT-ORDER-2025-1.pdf

value_label: Statutory limits on hours apply
note: At most 8 hours a day and 44 a week, 6 hours without a break, overtime at 1.5 times capped at 72 hours a month, and 12 hours a day in total; weekly rest day. The Commissioner may exempt employees from these limits (s 69). Domestic workers (BN-DW) differ: value 0.
source: Employment Order 2009 Part VII · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cap-278-2026-ed-employment-act.pdf

value_label: May change only on listed grounds, a limited number of times or with official approval
note: Transfer to another employer needs the worker's consent and the Commissioner's endorsement (s 24). The licence to employ immigrant workers is held by the employer (s 112), and the pass may name the employer, with the holder to stay in the specified job (reg 15). Company change-of-employer endorsements need a Labour Department transfer form. Domestic workers (BN-DW) differ: value 0.
source: Department of Labour · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cap-278-2026-ed-employment-act.pdf

value_label: May join but faces legal limits, or residence status makes membership largely theoretical
note: Same rules as for all workers: non-citizens may join, but may be officers only after 3 years of continuous service and residence in Brunei.
source: Trade Unions Act (Cap. 128) · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CAP-128-2023-TRADE-UNIONS-ACT.pdf

value_label: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
note: Same agency rules as for domestic workers: agencies may charge only the fees provided by the Order or regulations; the regulations prescribe only licence fees.
source: Employment Agencies Order 2004 · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/S-84-2004-E-%E2%80%8BEMPLOYMENT-AGENCIES-ORDER-2004.pdf

value_label: Only employer-bought private or accident insurance is required
note: Compulsory employer-bought medical insurance (at least $100,000; no wage deduction) and compulsory work-injury insurance with an approved insurer (Workmen's Compensation Act s 27; manual workers are covered whatever their pay).
source: Workmen's Compensation Act (Cap. 74) · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CAP-74-1984-ED-WORKMENS-COMPENSATION-ACT.pdf

value_label: Only general channels, or channels hard to reach from the workplace (for example at sea)
note: The Commissioner of Labour inquires into disputes of workmen and of employees earning up to $3,000 a month (Part 16). Complaint forms are in Malay and English; no dedicated multilingual migrant channel was found.
source: Department of Labour · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cap-278-2026-ed-employment-act.pdf

value_label: No route: fixed maximum stay, or time does not count
note: Employment Passes last at most 5 years at a time, renewable. Permanent-residence categories (updated 31 December 2024) are based on family ties or descent, not on employment.
source: Immigration Act (Cap. 17) · official guidance: https://www.immigration.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/GARISPANDUAN-DAN-SYARAT-SYARAT-KELAYAKAN-KATEGORI-KATEGORI-PERMOHONAN-UNTUK-MENDAPATKAN-TARAF-PENDUDUK-TETAP-NEGARA-BRUNEI-DARUSSALAM.pdf

value_label: Only in a later status or on conditions
note: The wife or dependent child of an Employment Pass holder may get a Dependant's Pass at the Controller's discretion and against security; holders may not work without written consent. A husband is not covered.
source: Immigration Department · official text: https://www.agc.gov.bn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CAP-17-RG-1-IMMIGRATION-REGULATIONS.pdf
